app.name: Han Input
find.seo: Find a Chinese character through any input method, reading, shape, index or encoding, and combine what you know until one remains.
methods.seo: Every input method for Chinese characters, including Cangjie, Wubi and kana, with the codes each one gives and a page to type in it.
readings.seo: Search the historical, dialect and foreign readings of 漢字音典 across more than 3,000 varieties, and type in any of them.
rhymes.seo: The Guangyun as a rhyme table: rhymes down the side, initials across the top, grade and tone in every row.
radicals.seo: The 214 Kangxi radicals by residual strokes, each listing the characters written under it.
convert.seo: Convert the private-use codes of old Taiwanese and Hakka fonts to Unicode, and browse every recorded mapping.
composition.seo: Convert Taiwan's pre-IDS composition formulas and arithmetic composition to IDS, with each database's signs kept distinct.
about.seo: Where every table on Han Input comes from, the terms each carries and the limits of what it records.

composition.title: Old composition formulas
composition.intro: Taiwan's 漢字構形資料庫 used thirteen symbols; arithmetic composition writes characters with signs whose meanings differ by database. The Korean History Database and CBETA use different assignments, so pick one. Shape markers give their parts, and signs that leave a position open are marked.
composition.hint: Connectors sit between parts; a repeat goes before its part.
composition.arithmetic.title: Arithmetic composition
composition.arithmetic.intro: Several East Asian databases write characters with arithmetic signs, and the signs mean different things in each. Choose a notation; the rules table gives its signs.
composition.arithmetic.placeholder: Paste a formula, or use a sign above
composition.arithmetic.searchHint: Search finds characters that contain these parts; the exact structure is not required.
composition.arithmetic.note.combine: * says only that the parts combine; the IDS uses overlap ⿻.
composition.arithmetic.note.contain: @ says only that one part contains the other; the IDS uses ⿴.
composition.arithmetic.note.replace: -+ removes a part and adds another; the IDS overlaps the remainder and the addition with ⿻.
composition.arithmetic.note.unknown: ? is an unknown part; it is written as ? and left out of the search parts.
composition.arithmetic.note.variant: ▼ marks a variant record and is left out of the IDS.
composition.arithmetic.note.separator: [] marks a formula inside running text; only its contents are read.
composition.arithmetic.problem.unexpecte: A grouping sign does not match.
composition.arithmetic.problem.trailing: The formula has text after its end.
composition.arithmetic.source.korean: Korean History Database, 파자 검색 help
composition.arithmetic.source.general: CBETA, 一般組字式基本規則
composition.arithmetic.citation: Korean signs follow the Korean History Database 破字 help (국사편찬위원회); the general signs follow CBETA’s rules for assembled rare characters.
composition.placeholder: Paste an old formula, or use a symbol above
composition.parts: Parts after · keep their writing order. The old shape marker does not record their arrangement.
composition.problem.orphan: A connector has no part before it.
composition.problem.missing: A connector has no part after it.
composition.problem.repeat-missing: A repetition has no part after it.
composition.problem.mixed: The formula mixes connectors; only one kind may be used.
composition.problem.shape-connect: A connector appears inside a shape marker.
composition.problem.shape-chain: A shape marker cannot be joined with a connector.
composition.problem.shape-open: A shape marker is not closed.
composition.problem.shape-empty: A shape marker has no parts.
composition.problem.nested-shape: A shape marker appears inside another.
composition.source.citation: Symbols and shapes follow 莊德明, 〈構字式的處理技巧〉, 中央研究院資訊科學研究所, 2007.
